source.title: Large Batch Training Does Not Need Warmup
source.authors: Zhou-Yuan Huo; Bin Gu; Heng Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training-loss results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, including comparisons between large-batch optimizers and warmup settings. Those results concern optimization and convergence but do not test the claim’s classification-error versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training loss, test accuracy, and epochs to specified training-loss thresholds. It does not report training classification error, corrupted or random-label fitting, bad-local-minimum rates, or the claim’s other named conditions. Its references to prior results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests large-batch optimizers, learning-rate scaling and warmup removal, but none of V1–V6. It reports neither training classification error nor the required width, depth, initialization, stability-threshold or normalization comparisons. Generic divergence at large learning rates does not establish V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that CLARS removes the need for warmup in their large-batch experiments and converges faster than LARS. They also claim a fine-grained convergence analysis supporting their method and explaining large-batch heuristics.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes CLARS, a layer-wise adaptive optimizer, and compares it with LARS and mNAG. It evaluates warmup removal and large-batch convergence rather than the claim’s initialization, capacity, or training-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Results are presented for different architectures, datasets, batch sizes, warmup durations, and learning-rate settings; the text reports mNAG divergence on VGG11/CIFAR-10 at batch size 8192.

fits_no_version.finding: CLARS without warmup outperforms warmup LARS in the reported CIFAR-10 and ImageNet comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested large-batch recipes, CLARS can remove warmup and improve convergence relative to LARS, with optimizer-specific eta choices.

fits_no_version.finding: mNAG diverges on VGG11/CIFAR-10 at batch size 8192.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested large-batch mNAG recipe can diverge on VGG11.

fits_no_version.finding: LARS gives similar convergence in epochs across batch sizes 128–8192 with linear learning-rate scaling and warmup.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise adaptive optimization can preserve convergence in epochs as batch size increases under the tested schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-specific learning-rate sweeps produce different times to training-loss thresholds and different divergence boundaries in fixed architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Useful learning-rate ranges differ across layers in the tested sigmoid networks and ResNet8.

record.problems: For the relevant experiments, several outcomes are shown only in figures without tabulated numerical values; reported comparisons emphasize loss and testing accuracy, not training classification error. The text reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure-based values are retained as qualitative/figure-only rows where the text gives the model, setting, and stated outcome.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on capacity or training recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons and the specified initialization alternatives.
Initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above an initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch normalization's effect on speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The batch-normalization argument in Section 3.4 is attributed to Santurkar et al.; it supplies no new normalization comparison. Learning-rate bounds in the convergence analysis are sufficient conditions, not measurements of the initial linearized stability limit in V5. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error by depth, and shortcut, special initialization, or normalization comparisons as specified.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer plain CNN training.
Training at rates above a stability threshold, curvature/sharpness dynamics, squared-loss recovery, and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup normalization comparisons.

rows.subject: ResNet56
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LARS at batch size 8192 and compared with smaller-batch LARS and mNAG.
rows.measure: Top-1 testing accuracy; training loss is shown in Figure 2.
rows.note: Text says LARS convergence rates from batch sizes 128 to 8192 are similar; the figure does not provide extracted numerical values. Training classification error is not reported.
rows.check: Figure 2 displays testing accuracy and a learning-rate schedule; despite its caption, it supplies no training-loss panel. The baseline should identify the smaller-batch LARS runs and mNAG comparator.

rows.subject: mNAG
rows.operation_detail: Trained on VGG11 using mNAG at large batch size; the authors state that it diverged.
rows.value: mNAG even diverges in training VGG11 using CIFAR-10.
rows.note: Explicit text reports divergence; no classification-error value is given.
rows.check: The subject is VGG11; mNAG is its optimizer, not a model. Divergence is explicitly reported, but no initial stability threshold is measured, so it cannot determine V5.

rows.subject: ResNet56
rows.operation_detail: Compared LARS with gradual warmup against CLARS without warmup.
rows.measure: Training loss and Top-1 testing accuracy
rows.value: CLARS always outperforms LARS by a large margin.
rows.note: Authors report the comparison qualitatively; no numerical training classification error is reported.
rows.check: This is the proposed optimizer's performance comparison, not evidence for a listed version. The condition omits that eta was tuned separately for both methods.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Compared CLARS without warmup with LARS using warmup and polynomial decay.
rows.measure: Training loss and Top-1 testing accuracy
rows.value: CLARS algorithm always converges much faster than the state-of-the-art large-batch optimizer LARS on advanced neural networks.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; training classification error is not reported.
rows.check: This is the proposed optimizer's performance comparison. Record eta = 0.001 for LARS versus 0.01 for CLARS, and effective batch size 16384 obtained by accumulating 32 batches of 512.
